paper_title: OpenAssistant Conversations -- Democratizing Large Language Model   Alignment
caption: Left: Relative share of the most frequent languages in the dataset. Right: Distribution of contributions among users.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the relative share of the most frequent languages in the OpenAssistant Conversations dataset. The chart is divided into eight segments, each representing a different language or category, with percentages indicating their proportion of the total. The largest segment, colored in dark blue, represents English at 42.8%. The second largest, in a lighter blue, is Spanish at 31.4%. Following these are Russian at 5.7%, German at 3.6%, French at 2.9%, Chinese at 2.5%, Thai at 1.7%, and Portuguese (Brazil) at 1.6%. The smallest segment, labeled "Other" and colored in light gray, accounts for 5.8%. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right, with the largest segments (English and Spanish) occupying the left and bottom portions of the chart. Labels and percentages are clearly displayed within or adjacent to each slice, and the chart uses varying shades of blue and gray to distinguish between categories. There is no visible legend, but the labels are directly associated with their respective slices.
